jobs.title: Executive Assistant, Office of the CEO
jobs.description:
Founded in 1977 as the Senior Care Action Network, SCAN began with a simple but radical idea: that older adults deserve to stay healthy and independent. That belief was championed by a group of community activists we still honor today as the “12 Angry Seniors.” Their mission continues to guide everything we do.


Today, SCAN is a nonprofit health organization serving more than 500,000 people across Arizona, California, Nevada, New Mexico, Texas, and Washington, with over $8 billion in annual revenue. With nearly five decades of experience, we have built a distinctive, values\-driven platform dedicated to improving care for older adults.


Our work spans Medicare Advantage, fully integrated care models, primary care, care for the most medically and socially complex populations, and next\-generation care delivery models. Across all of this, we are united by a shared commitment: combining compassion with discipline, innovation with stewardship, and growth with integrity.


At SCAN, we believe scale should strengthen—not dilute—our mission. We are building the future of care for older adults, grounded in purpose, accountability, and respect for the people and communities we serve.

 **The Job**


As an Executive Assistant in the CEO Office, you'll play a pivotal role in our dynamic organization. Your role will not only ensure the smooth operation of the executive office as it relates to all Board activities and other administrative responsibilities as necessary. You will be instrumental in driving the achievement of our organization’s vision, mission, and strategic objectives by providing unparalleled support to the Office of the CEO.

 **You Will**

**Administrative Support Maven:** Deliver comprehensive administrative support to the CEO Office in respect of all Board events, logistics, and activities. Manage complex calendars, schedule meetings, prioritize and respond to emails, and handle sensitive information with utmost discretion. Ensure a seamless flow of activities, including meticulous preparation and planning time. Collaborate with other assistants or independently manage meeting schedules, travel arrangements, event management, and external commitments. Maintain confidential department files and ensure the Board is fully prepared for all engagements.

**Event Coordination Extraordinaire:** Plan and coordinate high\-level meetings and events, ensuring all logistics are flawlessly handled.

**Travel Management Guru:** Arrange detailed travel itineraries, including flights, accommodation, transportation, and related activities, ensuring a hassle\-free travel experience.

**Project Management Prodigy:** Assist in the planning and execution of strategic initiatives and special projects as directed by the CEO and Chief of Staff. Develop efficient procedures to manage and track the status of materials and documents for distribution.

**Meeting Support Specialist:** Collect and prepare draft agendas, prioritize items in consultation with executives, finalize agendas, disseminate meeting materials, coordinate meeting records, evaluations, and follow\-up reports.

**Community of Practice Leader:** Lead and facilitate a community of practice with other executive assistants. Foster collaboration, share best practices, and promote professional development among peers.

**Office Management Maestro:** Assist with the administration of the executive office Board calendar and events, ensuring an organized, efficient, and welcoming work environment.

**Brand Management Ambassador:** Ensure consistent and cohesive brand representation internally and externally.


We seek Rebels who are curious about AI and its power to transform how we operate and serve our members.


Actively support the achievement of SCAN’s Vision and Goals.


Other duties as assigned.

* Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration, Communications, or a related field, or equivalent experience
* Minimum of 4 years of experience supporting C\-suite executives or a CEO, preferably in a large corporate setting.
* Proven ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously with high accuracy and keen attention to detail.
* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (including CoPilot).
* Demonstrated ability to lead and mentor a team or community of practice.
* High degree of professionalism, emotional intelligence, and curiosity.
* Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise discretion.
* Strong problem\-solving skills and the ability to anticipate and address needs proactively.

* Base Pay Range: $80,000\.00\- $100,000\.00 annually
* Work Mode: Mostly Onsite (In office 2 days per week on Tuesday/Wednesday)
* An annual employee bonus program
* Robust Wellness Program
* Generous paid\-time\-off (PTO) along with 11 paid holidays per year, 1 floating holiday, birthday off, and 2 volunteer days
* Excellent 401(k) Retirement Saving Plan with employer match
* Robust employee recognition program
* Tuition reimbursement
* An opportunity to become part of a team that makes a difference to our members and our community every day!

  

We're always looking for talented people to join our team! Qualified applicants are encouraged to apply now!

jobs.description:
**Aunt Lute Books Co\-Executive Director in Administration Job Posting**

**About the Organization**

Aunt Lute Books is a 44\-year\-old non profit, intersectional feminist press dedicated to publishing literature by writers who have traditionally been underrepresented or excluded from the literary canon. For more than four decades, Aunt Lute has championed bold, boundary\-pushing fiction, to create space for voices and perspectives too often marginalized within mainstream publishing.

**About the Position**

Aunt Lute is seeking a motivated and collaborative **Co\-Executive Director in Administration** to help co\-lead the organization through its next stage of growth and sustainability. This part\-time position (20\-22 hours per week) works in partnership with the Co\-Executive Director in Operations. The Co\-Executive Director in Administration will focus primarily on fundraising, grant writing and resource development, financial oversight, organizational growth and strategic planning, community engagement and Board relations. They will uphold Aunt Lute’s mission and values in their leadership and decision\-making. This is a hybrid position based in San Francisco. Ideally, candidates should be able to work in\-person once a week and attend events.

*\*See Addendum below for Co\-Executive Director in Operations responsibilities.*

**Job Responsibilities:**

Development

* In collaboration with the Board of Directors, creating and implementing fundraising plans that primarily focus on private foundations and individual annual donors.
* Working closely with staff and Board to accomplish revenue goals consisting of major gifts, foundation and government grants.

Financial Management

* Having a daily knowledge of where financial matters stand for the organization, which includes providing transparent fiscal stewardship that maintains a positive financial position and adequate control and accounting of all funds.
* Develop and propose an annual budget to the Board for their approval.
* Working with our accounting consultant to reconcile accounts and to write tax reports including city, state, and federal reports as required.

Organizational Growth

* With the Board of Directors, creating short\- and long\-term strategic plans in support of Aunt Lute’s mission and documenting progress towards achieving them.
* Developing and improving organizational infrastructure, including business processes, systems, policies, and tools, to maximize efficiency and future growth.

Community Engagement/Outreach

* Participating in relevant community events and cultivating speaking skills to deepen local networks, engage new donors, and expand community presence.
* Developing and nurturing positive relationships with other arts and cultural organizations.
* Supporting staff in planning and executing events sponsored by Aunt Lute in partnership with mission\-aligned organizations.
* Practice feminist leadership styles and ability to engage with racial/gender equity organizations.

Staff Management

* Work with the Co\-ED in Operations to manage the recruitment, employment, and release of all personnel while implementing sound human resource practices.
* Co\-managing the oversight of employee performance and delegating responsibilities.
* Promoting a work culture that is inclusive, equitable, transparent, and respectful of all backgrounds and identities.

Board Relations

* Support the board in recruiting and identifying prospective members who bring diverse skills, perspectives, and strong commitment to Aunt Lute’s mission.
* Maintaining regular communication with the Board Chair through regular check\-ins, and attending and supporting preparation for Board meetings, held every other month to advance organizational priorities and implement strategic planning.
* Providing leadership in developing program, organizational, and financial plans with the Board.

**Required Skills for this Position:**

Required skills and qualifications:

* 3 or more years in non\-profit organizational management within publishing, literary arts, or cultural organizations
* 3 years of experience in managing budgets; considerable experience working with spreadsheets (Microsoft Excel)
* Experience in grant writing, fundraising, and donor relations
* Demonstrated commitment to equitable and transparent collaboration with colleagues
* Highly competent in verbal, written, and visual communication
* Proximity to or ability to commute to the Bay Area for in\-person meetings and events

Preferred skills and qualifications:

* Experience working with a nonprofit Board of Directors
* Experience with fundraising tech platforms
* Knowledgeable with Social Media and Publicity
* Experience with QuickBooks

**Compensation:**

* $34\-$38/hour for 20 hours per week

**How to Apply:** 

Email a resume and cover letter addressed to Aunt Lute Search Committee to jobs@auntlute.com*.* 

Cover letters should address how applicants believe their qualifications, experience, aspirations, and values align with Aunt Lute’s publishing mission. Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026, and applications will be accepted until the position is filled. If selected for an interview, candidates will be asked to complete an online questionnaire and provide references.

**\*Addendum**

**The Co\-Executive Director in Operations is responsible for:**

* Accounts payable, receivable, banking, and account reconciliation
* Working with the accountant on account reconciliation and end of the year reporting.
* Reporting to the accountant as they close the financial year: on payroll, inventory, sales, etc.
* Payroll and related financial reporting
* Book inventory management, reprints, and shipping
* Serving as liaison with Aunt Lute’s distributor, Ingram
* Overseeing royalty calculations
* Coordinating logistics for book fairs, events, and conferences
* Reporting to the Board on forthcoming book releases, sales, cash and investments, and other operational matter

**GHJ is looking for a** **High Net Worth (HNW) Tax Managing Director**


**WHY we get up in the morning**



At GHJ, we foster a flexible, entrepreneurial environment so our people achieve their personal and professional goals.



Our success is driven by retaining the best, diverse talent. We invest in our people and technology to deepen firm expertise and fuel sustainable growth. And we partner with our clients locally and globally to deliver innovative solutions.


**WHAT we believe**



GHJ works side by side with business leaders and nonprofit organizations to deliver responsive, high\-impact advisory, tax and accounting solutions that drive real results. Headquartered in Los Angeles with offices in Buffalo, Denver, Orange County and San Jose and backed by our own dispersed workforce, GHJ meets clients where they are to help leaders achieve their strategic goals.


**THRIVING On Our Own Terms**



We are deeply committed to our core values of Bright Minds, Brave Hearts and Bold Actions and incorporate them into every aspect of our business. By living these values, GHJ measures success by the strength of our relationships, the quality of our impact and the integrity of our actions. The Firm’s independence allows us to make strategic choices to innovate, invest and evolve with purpose. Ultimately, GHJ values operational excellence, financial discipline and the courage to prioritize sustainability over size.


**Summary of Role:**

GHJ is seeking an accomplished High Net Worth (HNW) Tax professional with deep experience in serving high net worth individuals and their related entities.



This position reports to the Tax Department Practice Leader.



The Tax HNW Managing Director will be responsible for leading client engagements requiring individual, trust and gift tax expertise. The ideal candidate will have advanced technical skills in a variety of tax areas, along with well\-developed and demonstrated management and supervisory skills. Administrative, leadership, and business development responsibilities are also key elements for this position.


### **You will be responsible for:**



The Tax HNW Managing Director is responsible for the efficient, accurate, complete, and timely preparation of all clients' tax returns whether prepared personally or by supervision of others. Advanced technical skills in a variety of tax and accounting areas, along with well\-developed and applied management and supervisory skills, are required. Responsibilities include:


* Managing the preparation and review of individual, trust and gift tax returns for high net worth individuals and their families;
* Performing technical tax review and approval of all tax returns of any complexity;
* Participating in client meetings and tax planning efforts for a variety of clients;
* Acting as a resource for tax preparers/specialists on specific tax issues and/or questions;
* Communicating to the appropriate firm personnel important tax and tax developments affecting the firm's clients;
* Managing governmental tax examinations; may represent the client before the appropriate taxing authorities;
* Supervising tax staff and providing on\-the\-job training;
* Working to develop responsible, trained staff by assisting in recruiting, performance evaluations, developing training aids, and acting as an instructor in professional development programs;
* Maintaining a knowledge of general economic and political trends of possible tax or other legislation that could affect the business climate;
* Participating in firm's practice development efforts through involvement with referral sources, community and industry activities.
### **What we need from you:**


* 10\+ years of experience in public accounting (tax), demonstrating a proven ability in handling tax complexity, scope, and research.
* Prior leadership of client engagements and supervisory experience of managers and staff.
* Required exposure to Forms 1040 (Individual return), 1041 (trust return), 1065 (partnership/LLC return), 1120S (S corporation return), and 709 (gift return).
* Experience with forms 5227 (Split Interest Trust Information return) and 706 (Estate return) would be a plus.
* Excellent oral \& written communication skills.
* Self\-starter with the ability to work independently and use good judgment.
* Strong interpersonal skills
* Creative thinker with entrepreneurial approach to client interactions, including tax planning and bringing value to clients.
* Willingness to lead firm or tax department initiatives and be seen as a leader in the tax department.
### **What skills \& experience you’ll bring to us:**


* Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Business, or related equivalent.
* Masters of Science degree in Taxation or a J.D. highly preferred
* CPA certification or active law license required.


**Seven decades, one enduring focus: our people and our clients.**



GHJ is a national independent advisory, tax and accounting firm that partners with businesses and nonprofit organizations to deliver clarity and confidence. Since 1953, GHJ has combined deep industry expertise with an entrepreneurial spirit to help leaders achieve their strategic goals.



GHJ is headquartered in Los Angeles and serves clients nationwide, backed by its own dispersed workforce. With nearly 300 professionals and 25\+ partners, the Firm provides senior\-level expertise with deep industry capabilities in food and beverage, media and advertising, entertainment and nonprofit.



GHJ is a top\-ranking firm in the U.S. and member of HLB International. Through this global network, GHJ offers seamless access to resources in over 150 countries while remaining fiercely focused on client success.

jobs.description:
Join the transformative team at City of Hope, where we're changing lives and making a real difference in the fight against cancer, diabetes, and other life\-threatening illnesses. City of Hope’s growing national system includes its Los Angeles campus, a network of clinical care locations across Southern California, a new cancer center in Orange County, California, and treatment facilities in Atlanta, Chicago and Phoenix. Our dedicated and compassionate employees are driven by a common mission: To deliver the cures of tomorrow to the people who need them today.


The Executive Director, Professional and Academic Services is a senior administrative leader within the Physician Enterprise responsible for advancing the strategic, operational, academic, research, financial, and administrative priorities of academic departments and centers. Serving as the primary administrative executive partner to Department Chairs and Center Directors, this leader will drive performance, strengthen infrastructure, guide resource decisions, and ensure alignment with institutional strategy and Physician Enterprise goals. This highly visible position collaborates with senior clinical, administrative, and system leaders to support coordinated decision\-making, disciplined execution, and measurable results across 11 academic departments and two centers.

**As a successful candidate, you will:**

* Provide executive leadership and accountability for administrative operations across multiple academic departments and centers.
* Serve as a strategic partner to Department Chairs and Center Directors, advising on priorities, performance, resources, risks, and growth opportunities.
* Establish governance structures, operating expectations, and performance measures that strengthen clinical, academic, research, financial, and administrative outcomes.
* Oversee academic and faculty affairs, including research administration, faculty appointments, promotions, mentorship, development, and institutional compliance.
* Direct departmental financial performance across operating budgets, grants, philanthropy, research compensation, clinical revenue, and other funding sources.
* Lead the administrative strategy for physician and physician\-scientist recruitment, onboarding, integration, and retention.
* Provide executive oversight of physician practice performance, including access, productivity, quality, professional billing, APP utilization, clinical trial accrual, and operational effectiveness.
* Sponsor business plans, resource proposals, and improvement initiatives that advance care delivery, physician program performance, academic productivity, and organizational effectiveness.
* Mentor and develop department administrators and other administrative leaders while fostering accountability, collaboration, and high performance.
* Guide space, facilities, technology, equipment, and infrastructure planning in support of institutional growth and operational priorities.
**Your qualifications should include:**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, science, or a related field.
* At least 10 years of business management experience in an academic research or healthcare environment.
* Seven to 10 years of progressively responsible management experience.
* Demonstrated experience with budget development, grant management, space planning, and personnel management.
* Strong knowledge of management and accounting principles within a research, scientific, medical, or healthcare environment.
* Ability to analyze complex administrative and financial data, develop meaningful reports, and create effective solutions to short\- and long\-term business challenges.
* Proven ability to lead through multiple layers of management and influence senior physician and administrative leaders.
* Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, and organizational communication skills.
* Demonstrated ability to work independently, establish priorities, identify issues, and ensure effective follow\-through.
* Master’s degree, MBA, or MHA preferred.


City of Hope employees’ pay is based on the following criteria: work experience, qualifications, and work location.


City of Hope is an equal opportunity employer.

And it's why we need caring, committed people on our team \- like you. Join us on our mission to heal humanity, one child and family at a time.

The Executive Director is responsible for staying up to date on all clinical and regulatory requirements and leads the execution of those requirements across the enterprise.


The Executive Director fills an executive sponsorship role where they partner with key constituents across the enterprise to represent the Center for Advanced Practice. They actively contribute to strategic decisions to ensure that those decisions align with the Center for Advanced Practice strategic mission and vision.


Examples of key partnerships could include but are not limited to divisions, human resources, marketing, medical staffing, finance, strategy, process improvement, quality improvement, academic clinical partnerships, and a variety of other clinical, operational, and strategic committees.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Corporate Communications
jobs.description:
### **About Teneo**


Teneo is the global CEO advisory firm. We partner with our clients globally to do great things for a better future.


Drawing upon our global team and expansive network of senior advisors, we provide advisory services across our five business segments on a stand\-alone or fully integrated basis to help our clients solve complex business challenges. Our clients include a significant number of the Fortune 100 and FTSE 100, as well as other corporations, financial institutions and organizations.


Our full range of advisory services includes strategic communications, investor relations, financial transactions and restructuring, management consulting, physical and cyber risk, organizational design, board and executive search, geopolitics and government affairs, corporate governance and ESG.


The firm has more than 1,800 employees located in 50\+ offices around the world.


### **The Opportunity**


Teneo's San Francisco office is in a building phase. We are assembling a small, senior team of advisors who understand how technology companies actually work: their customers, investors, boards, and regulators, and the internal dynamics their leaders have to navigate. We help these companies through moments of significant transition. The Managing Director will work with the San Francisco Office head to lead the office's Strategy \& Communications team, own a portfolio of client relationships, and play a central role in growing the office's business and reputation in the Bay Area. This is a chance to help shape an office and a practice, not just step into one.


We are also looking for someone who believes the communications function itself is changing. Our clients are rethinking what communications means inside their companies: how it connects to strategy, how it is structured and staffed, and how new tools, including AI, are changing the work. We want an MD who can help clients lead that evolution and who is eager to help Teneo do the same.


### **Who We're Looking For**


The strongest candidates will be builders. Many will have held senior in\-house roles at technology companies, where they built or rebuilt teams, processes, and systems, and learned to advise across internal silos because they had to operate inside them. We equally value agency and advisory leaders who have built something of their own, such as a practice, an office, or a new offering, and who bring real empathy for the operator's seat. Either way, you understand that good counsel starts with knowing a client's world, not just the outcome they want.


### **Responsibilities**


* Work with the San Francisco Office Head to lead the San Francisco Strategy \& Communications team. Set direction, develop talent, provide senior\-level oversight across engagements, and help recruit the people who will grow the office.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to founders, CEOs, and senior leaders, influencing client direction and building long\-term relationships.
* Drive business development. Originate new client relationships, expand existing ones, and turn the office's network into client work.
* Help clients through moments of transition, including fundraising, IPO readiness, leadership changes, M\&A, regulatory scrutiny, crises, and shifts in business model or technology. Translate the realities of a technology business for the audiences that judge it.
* Develop and lead complex, integrated communications programs that use every lever together: earned media, owned and social channels, executive visibility, events, and non\-traditional media such as podcasts, newsletters, and online video.
* Advise clients on how their communications function should evolve, including its structure, capabilities, operating model, and use of new tools.
* Build Teneo's presence in the Bay Area through thought leadership, signature events, speaking, and relationships across the technology, investor, and business communities.
* Partner with colleagues across Teneo's segments, including management consulting, investor relations, financial advisory, risk, and executive search, to deliver integrated solutions.
* Help the office experiment with and adopt AI\-enabled ways of working, in partnership with Teneo's firmwide AI efforts.
* Make complex decisions affecting colleagues and clients in a timely and transparent way, and foster a culture where quality and client satisfaction come first.

### **Qualifications**


* 15\+ years of relevant experience in corporate communications, public relations, media, or a related field.
* A track record of building teams, functions, practices, processes, or systems, ideally including leading an organization through significant transformation.
* Senior in\-house communications experience at a technology company is strongly preferred. Agency and advisory leaders with deep technology\-client experience are also encouraged to apply.
* Significant experience independently leading large, complex client engagements.
* Experience counseling senior executives and boards, and working alongside external financial and legal advisors.
* Deep familiarity with the technology ecosystem, particularly founders of mid\- to late\-stage startups, with strong relationships across both traditional and non\-traditional media.
* A holistic view of communications as a driver of business outcomes.
* Curiosity about AI and hands\-on use of AI tools in your own work.
* Comfort with ambiguity and the pace of building something new.
* Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
* Available to work from Teneo's San Francisco office at least three days a week.

Iowa Public Health Association (IPHA) is a statewide nonprofit membership organization and an aﬀiliated association of the American Public Health Association (APHA). Our mission is to unite and strengthen the voice for public health in Iowa. Our strategic goals center around 1\) Membership Structure \& Benefits; 2\) Advocacy; 3\) Organizational Capacity; and 4\) Supporting \& Connecting Community Partners.

We work hard to set the tone for evidence\-based policy decisions at the state and local levels by serving as a nonpartisan resource for elected officials, advocates, practitioners, and the public. We strive to be the independent voice for public health.

The incoming Executive Director will lead an organization that is currently in sound financial condition, has a strong and dedicated 12\-member Board, and more than 500 members. IPHA is involved in several programs and initiatives aligned with its 2026\-2029 Strategic Plan and is a well\-respected organization. More information can be found at www.iowapha.org .

**PRIMARY FUNCTION:**

This position contributes to IPHA's growth and success by developing people and programs and growing and managing resources. IPHA is searching for a dynamic leader with a proven track record of growing and leading a membership association. The Executive Director will lead the organization in partnership with the Board of Directors, staff, members, and contractors by providing a strategic vision and direction for the organization and developing long\-term organizational strategy. The position is responsible for achieving the organization's purpose as reflected in its mission and vision.

**Mission:** Uniting and strengthening the voice for public health in Iowa.

**Vision:** A healthy and thriving Iowa because of the strong foundation laid by public health.

**DUTIES \& RESPONSIBILITIES:**  
**Executive Leadership (40%)**

* Lead the development and execution of the organization's strategic plan, setting clear goals and priorities to guide long\-term growth.
* Manage day\-to\-day operations and implement IPHA's strategic priorities by overseeing daily functions and turning long\-term goals into actionable plans.
* Work closely with the Board of Directors, committees, volunteers, staff, and contractors to ensure clear communication, strong collaboration, and shared accountability across the organization.
* Identify opportunities to strengthen and grow the organization by evaluating new programs, partnerships, and resources that align with IPHA's mission.
* Drive development and grant writing efforts. Work with the Board of Directors on sponsorships, donors, as well as membership recruitment, support, and retention.

**Advocacy \& Public Policy Leadership (30%)**

* Serve as IPHA's registered lobbyist, manage relationships with contract lobbyist, and represent IPHA's interests with the Legislature and state agencies.
* Lead the Board's annual advocacy prioritization process and serve as chief spokesperson to media, members, partners, and the public.
* Coordinate the Advocacy Committee, with regular updates to the Board, to promote public health policy priorities and elevate IPHA's presence as the independent voice for public health.
* Advocate for and safeguard federal, state, and local funding for both public health programs and workforce by building strategic partnerships across Iowa and nationally \- working to secure new resources for the state while protecting existing public health investments.

**Membership, Relationship Building \& Workforce Development (20%)**

* Grow membership recruitment, engagement, and retention by driving strategies that attract new members and strengthen long\-term retention.

	+ Solicits assigned donors for gifts of $25,000 and more to meet organizational priorities and annual projected fundraising revenue goals.
	+ In collaboration with the Sr. Managing Director, Chief Advancement Officer (CAO) and other Advancement Team members, identifies and pursues new prospects, developing and implementing a clear strategy for each prospect, leading to new and increased giving over time by connecting donor philanthropic priorities with Sierra Club’s programs and priorities.

	+ Drives strategies and plans to identify, cultivate, upgrade and/or solicit new donors, with an eye towards building a strong pipeline of qualified major donors and high\-net\-worth individuals with the capacity to give $25,000 or greater.

Home to over 1\.9 million people, Broward County is located between Palm Beach and Miami\-Dade counties, forming the center of South Florida’s largest metropolitan area in which 6\.1 million people reside. Within the County’s approximate 1,200 square miles are 31 municipalities, the largest of which is the county seat, Fort Lauderdale. About two\-thirds of Broward County is part of the undeveloped Everglades conservation area. Broward County boasts 23 miles of pristine Atlantic coastline, and its beaches attract both the local population as well as tourists from around the world. With an average year\-round temperature of 76 degrees, Broward County has a tropical climate and is a choice destination for over nineteen million visitors every year.
  

  

Broward County’s warm climate, demographic diversity, robust and expanding economy, top\-rated schools, colleges and universities, cutting\-edge healthcare, and an advanced transportation system afford its residents an exceptional quality of life. Broward offers world\-class dining, high\-quality theater, cosmopolitan nightlife, and premium shopping venues, as well as an abundance of recreational activities such as golf, pickleball, soccer, deep\-sea fishing, boating and vast opportunities for fun on the beach.
  

  

The Fort Lauderdale\-Hollywood International Airport is in Broward County and is less than two miles from Port Everglades where most major cruise lines use as a homeport. Among Broward County’s abundant retail shopping options is Sawgrass Mills, the largest one\-story value retail shopping mall in the United States. For the sports enthusiast, Broward County is home to the National Hockey League’s Florida Panthers, while the National Basketball Association’s Miami Heat, the Major League Baseball’s Miami Marlins, and the National Football League’s Miami Dolphins are just a short drive or quick train ride away.  

  

**The County Government**
  

The Broward County government was established under Charter in 1975 as a home\-rule government. The County has a Council/Manager form of government. The Broward County Board of County Commissioners is composed of nine members, elected every two years for four\-year staggered terms. Commissioners are voted to the position by their district constituents through partisan elections. The Mayor and Vice\-Mayor are Commission members annually elected by the Commission for one\-year terms. The Commission appoints the County Administrator, the County Attorney, and the County Auditor.
  

  

The County Administrator serves as the Chief Executive Officer and manages the County’s six major operating departments: Transportation, Aviation, Finance and Administrative Services, Human Services, Port Everglades, and Public Works and Environmental Services; eight offices and three divisions, which all together comprise over 70 lines of business.  

  

The County has nearly 6,700 employees and eight organized bargaining units. The County budget for FY26 is $8\.75 billion of which $5\.45 billion is Operating, $2\.55 billion is Capital and $0\.76 billion is Debt Service. The budget reflects strategic investments in transit, the seaport and airport, and many other critical services to residents.

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

  

The Oklahoma Tobacco Settlement Endowment Trust seeks an exceptional executive leader to serve as its Executive Director and lead one of Oklahoma's most distinctive public institutions.  



  

Created by a vote of the people of Oklahoma in 2000, TSET is entrusted with converting the certified earnings of the state's tobacco settlement endowment into strategic grants that improve the health and well\-being of Oklahomans. Through statewide programs, community grants, research, and evidence\-based initiatives, TSET works to and create lasting improvements in the health of Oklahoma communities.  



  

The Executive Director reports to the TSET Board of Directors and serves as the organization's chief executive, strategic leader, and principal administrative officer, responsible for translating the Board's vision, policies, and priorities into effective strategy, disciplined execution, and measurable results.  



  

This is more than an administrative leadership position. The Executive Director must lead at the intersection of public policy, public health, government, grantmaking, organizational management, and Board governance, and must understand how to operate effectively within a politically complex environment while preserving TSET's institutional integrity, credibility, statutory responsibilities, and long\-term mission.  



  

The successful candidate will bring exceptional executive judgment, political acumen, strategic thinking, financial stewardship including a comprehensive understanding of the financial statements of TSET, communication skill, and relationship building ability, equally comfortable advising a governing Board, leading a professional staff, engaging senior state leaders, working with public and private grantees, evaluating grant proposals, and representing TSET before diverse constituencies across Oklahoma.  



  

TSET's founders built this organization twenty\-five years ago in the truest entrepreneurial sense, establishing its systems, its credibility, and its impact largely at the same time it was already operating. Today, TSET enters a different season: a mature institution with a substantial endowment, an established track record, and significant resources to direct toward growth and innovation. The next Executive Director will need real leadership maturity: the ability to assess what the Board of Directors of TSET wants the Trust to become, recognize what has earned its place, and lead the organization through thoughtful renewal where it is warranted, bringing the same resourcefulness that built TSET together with the institutional discipline this next chapter demands, including an assessment of the necessary cultural changes to accomplish the future direction of TSET  



**About TSET**
--------------

TSET is a constitutionally protected public trust and, at the same time, a state agency, a grantmaker, a public health institution, and a steward of tobacco settlement certified earnings, governed by an appointed Board of Directors. By constitutional design, only the certified earnings on the Trust's investments, may be spent, and those earnings are directed toward clinical and basic research and treatment efforts in Oklahoma for the  



  

purpose of enhancing efforts to prevent and combat cancer and other tobacco\-related diseases, cost\-effective tobacco prevention and cessation programs, and other health related initiatives.  



  

**Vision and Mission:** Improving the health of every Oklahoman.  



  

TSET's giving is guided by five core principles: prioritizing evidence based and proven approaches; encouraging innovative and creative solutions; fostering collaborative relationships to maximize efficiency; supporting comprehensive services across both urban and rural Oklahoma; and awarding funding based on merit and public benefit. In practice, current strategic priorities span tobacco cessation, cancer research, healthcare access, workforce development, and prevention.  



  

TSET holds assets of approximately $2 billion and ranks among the state's largest health focused grantmakers, supporting roughly 100–150 active grants each year, typically $50,000 to $5 million per award, to universities, health systems, and community organizations. Signature initiatives include the Legacy Grants program, which awarded a combined $150 million to 14 grantee organizations, announced in 2025, and research grants, and efforts to promote tobacco cessation.

TSET's governance is divided between two boards. A separate, five\-member Board of Investors, chaired by the State Treasurer, is constitutionally responsible for investing the Trust's assets. The Director of Philanthropy is responsible for building and executing the Foundation's development strategy while identifying and advancing new avenues for organizational growth. This role blends traditional philanthropic development — major gifts, donor stewardship, and campaign leadership — with strategic business development, including new relationships, sponsorship opportunities, and the expansion of DMF's capacity\-building services to nonprofits across the region.

The Director of Philanthropy will work to diversify and grow fundraising efforts, deepen relationships with donors and community partners, and ensure that Giving Hearts Day, Lend A Hand Up, and DMF's other signature initiatives continue to scale sustainably. This is a high\-visibility, externally facing role well suited to a builder who is equally comfortable cultivating a major donor and shaping a growth strategy.

**Dakota Medical Foundation**

Since 1962, Dakota Medical Foundation (DMF) has connected people to opportunities that improve health across North Dakota and northwest Minnesota. Operating alongside its affiliate, Impact Foundation, DMF has invested more than $130 million in the region since 1996 and currently supports more than 500 nonprofit organizations through grantmaking, fundraising infrastructure, and capacity\-building programs.

DMF is best known as the founder and administrator of Giving Hearts Day, an annual 24\-hour regional giving event that has raised more than $257 million for local nonprofits since 2008\. The Foundation also leads Lend A Hand Up, providing financial assistance to families facing medical crises, and manages a portfolio of charitable funds, health and wellbeing initiatives, and partnerships with regional foundations including the North Dakota Dental Foundation, and the Optometric Foundation of North Dakota.

**Key Responsibilities**  
**Development Strategy \& Fundraising**

* Design and lead a comprehensive, multi\-year development strategy for multiple programs encompassing major gifts, planned giving, corporate and foundation partnerships, and annual giving.
* Build and manage a portfolio of major donor and institutional relationships, personally cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding key gifts.
* Manage the development team's annual fundraising goals and key performance metrics for multiple programs, reporting progress to the Leadership Team.
* Cultivate relationships with individuals, businesses, community foundations, and civic leaders to expand DMF's reach and impact across North Dakota and northwest Minnesota.
* Represent DMF publicly at community events, media engagements, and speaking opportunities to raise the Foundation's visibility and advance its mission.

**Team Leadership \& Organizational Collaboration** 

* Lead, coach, and grow the development team, with the expectation of building additional capacity as the function scales.
* Collaborate closely with the Leadership Team on fundraising forecasting, gift processing, and financial reporting, and on the operational execution of Giving Hearts Day and related events.
* Foster a culture of philanthropy and donor\-centered thinking across the organization, ensuring development priorities are integrated into DMF's broader program and communications strategies.

**Data, Systems \& Stewardship**

* Ensure the development team maintains timely and accurate donor records and gift tracking using DMF's CRM and fundraising systems.
* Manage metrics and reporting cadences that allow leadership and the Board to track fundraising performance, donor retention, and pipeline growth in real time.
* Oversee donor recognition, acknowledgment, and stewardship practices that reflect DMF's values and reinforce long\-term donor relationships.

**Qualifications**  
**Required**

* Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, business, communications, public health, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
* A minimum of 10 years of experience in nonprofit development, philanthropy, or business development.
* Demonstrated success building and executing development strategies that grow revenue and deepen donor relationships, ideally including experience with major gifts and campaign leadership.
* Proven ability to identify and act on new organizational growth opportunities, whether through partnerships, program expansion, or fundraising.
* Experience managing and developing a team, with strong skills in coaching, delegation, and cross\-functional collaboration.
* Excellent written, verbal, and public\-speaking communication skills, with the presence to represent the organization to donors, media, and community leaders.
* Willingness to travel regularly within North Dakota and northwest Minnesota and to work occasional evenings to promote Giving Hearts Day and Lend A Hand Up state\-wide.

**Preferred**

* Experience in a healthcare\-related, community foundation, or philanthropic organization.
* Familiarity with donor\-advised funds, community giving events, or regional philanthropic infrastructure comparable to Giving Hearts Day.
* CFRE (Certified Fundraising Executive) credential or equivalent professional certification.
* Existing relationships within the North Dakota / northwest Minnesota nonprofit, business, or healthcare community.

**Core Competencies**

* Strategic thinking with a bias toward execution
* Relationship\-driven, donor\-centered leadership
* Entrepreneurial mindset and comfort with ambiguity
* Collaborative, low\-ego approach to cross\-team leadership
* Sound judgment and discretion with confidential and financial information

Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter describing their interest in and qualifications for the Director of Philanthropy role to Elise Rue at erue@dakmed.org.

Dakota Medical Foundation is an Equal Opportunity Provider.

We work hard to set the tone for evidence\-based policy decisions at the state and local levels by serving as a nonpartisan resource for elected officials, advocates, practitioners, and the public. We strive to be the independent voice for public health.

The Director of Philanthropy is responsible for building and executing the Foundation's development strategy while identifying and advancing new avenues for organizational growth. This role blends traditional philanthropic development — major gifts, donor stewardship, and campaign leadership — with strategic business development, including new relationships, sponsorship opportunities, and the expansion of DMF's capacity\-building services to nonprofits across the region.

The Director of Philanthropy will work to diversify and grow fundraising efforts, deepen relationships with donors and community partners, and ensure that Giving Hearts Day, Lend A Hand Up, and DMF's other signature initiatives continue to scale sustainably. This is a high\-visibility, externally facing role well suited to a builder who is equally comfortable cultivating a major donor and shaping a growth strategy.

**Dakota Medical Foundation**

Since 1962, Dakota Medical Foundation (DMF) has connected people to opportunities that improve health across North Dakota and northwest Minnesota. Operating alongside its affiliate, Impact Foundation, DMF has invested more than $130 million in the region since 1996 and currently supports more than 500 nonprofit organizations through grantmaking, fundraising infrastructure, and capacity\-building programs.

DMF is best known as the founder and administrator of Giving Hearts Day, an annual 24\-hour regional giving event that has raised more than $257 million for local nonprofits since 2008\. The Foundation also leads Lend A Hand Up, providing financial assistance to families facing medical crises, and manages a portfolio of charitable funds, health and wellbeing initiatives, and partnerships with regional foundations including the North Dakota Dental Foundation, and the Optometric Foundation of North Dakota.

**Key Responsibilities**  
**Development Strategy \& Fundraising**

* Design and lead a comprehensive, multi\-year development strategy for multiple programs encompassing major gifts, planned giving, corporate and foundation partnerships, and annual giving.
* Build and manage a portfolio of major donor and institutional relationships, personally cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding key gifts.
* Manage the development team's annual fundraising goals and key performance metrics for multiple programs, reporting progress to the Leadership Team.
* Cultivate relationships with individuals, businesses, community foundations, and civic leaders to expand DMF's reach and impact across North Dakota and northwest Minnesota.
* Represent DMF publicly at community events, media engagements, and speaking opportunities to raise the Foundation's visibility and advance its mission.

**Team Leadership \& Organizational Collaboration** 

* Lead, coach, and grow the development team, with the expectation of building additional capacity as the function scales.
* Collaborate closely with the Leadership Team on fundraising forecasting, gift processing, and financial reporting, and on the operational execution of Giving Hearts Day and related events.
* Foster a culture of philanthropy and donor\-centered thinking across the organization, ensuring development priorities are integrated into DMF's broader program and communications strategies.

**Data, Systems \& Stewardship**

* Ensure the development team maintains timely and accurate donor records and gift tracking using DMF's CRM and fundraising systems.
* Manage metrics and reporting cadences that allow leadership and the Board to track fundraising performance, donor retention, and pipeline growth in real time.
* Oversee donor recognition, acknowledgment, and stewardship practices that reflect DMF's values and reinforce long\-term donor relationships.

**Qualifications**  
**Required**

* Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, business, communications, public health, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
* A minimum of 10 years of experience in nonprofit development, philanthropy, or business development.
* Demonstrated success building and executing development strategies that grow revenue and deepen donor relationships, ideally including experience with major gifts and campaign leadership.
* Proven ability to identify and act on new organizational growth opportunities, whether through partnerships, program expansion, or fundraising.
* Experience managing and developing a team, with strong skills in coaching, delegation, and cross\-functional collaboration.
* Excellent written, verbal, and public\-speaking communication skills, with the presence to represent the organization to donors, media, and community leaders.
* Willingness to travel regularly within North Dakota and northwest Minnesota and to work occasional evenings to promote Giving Hearts Day and Lend A Hand Up state\-wide.

**Preferred**
